note: The allow-list for every fill and stroke in assets/src/svg. The palette lint fails on any colour
not present in `colours`. Add a colour here, with a ramp, before any SVG uses it.
This file lives here. CLAUDE.md never named a canonical palette path, and a build-time input read
by the asset pipeline and by make verify-art - never by anything under app/ - belongs beside the
art it governs (same reasoning as assets/credits.json, ADR-0004). It is validated in place against
content/schemas/palette.schema.json by make validate-content, which also cross-checks that every
ramp tone and ink names a colour in `colours`.
UI, text and focus-ring colours are deliberately absent: ui-a11y owns those and they must pass WCAG AA.

shading.rule: Exactly three flat fills per material. No gradients, no dithering, no fourth tone. Author the BASE from the reference photograph, then derive light and shade with the formula below. Do not eyeball the other two tones.
shading.keyLight: Warm sun, upper left, 35 degrees above horizontal. One key for the whole game.

light.saturation: x1.00 if base S < 12 (neutral); x0.92 if S <= 45; x0.97 otherwise

shade.hueRotation: 12 degrees toward 225 (cool); toward 350 for the skin and hair families
shade.saturation: unchanged if base S < 12 (neutrals stay neutral); otherwise S + (92 - S) * 0.10

skin.why: Flesh shadow turns red-violet, not blue, and loses saturation. Without this, pale skin shadows go orange and deep skin highlights go ochre.

formula.colourSpace: HSL over sRGB, hue in degrees, S and L in percent.

acceptanceBand.note: 15 is what the formula produces. The floor is 8 rather than 15 because ramps whose base sits near L=8 or L=96 clamp: skin-6 and hair-black cannot span 15 twice without going to black. A ramp that clamps is correct; a ramp that was eyeballed flat is not.

shading.exemptionReason: Atmosphere ramps are vertical band sets, not a lit material, and snow clamps at white. They are authored by hand. The three insignia-rmc ramps are exempt for a different reason: they are not a lit material but the exact colours of an official artwork, the Royal Military College of Canada flag, reproduced unshaded and used by that one flag only (see ramps.insignia-rmc-flag.note).

outline.whyConstantWidth: Tapered strokes alias badly at atlas mip levels and cannot be expressed as a Rive shape stroke.
outline.colourRule: Use the ink whose hue family matches the character's largest colour area. Never #000000.
outline.backgroundSeparationRule: A background shape that does not read without a line has the wrong tone. Change the tone. Do not add a line.

ambientOcclusion.rule: Baked as soft shapes in the SVG, never as a runtime filter: the Canvas visual tier has no Filters (slice-1 task 1.19). AO goes where forms meet the ground and where parts overlap, nowhere else.

sky.note: Band order top to bottom is shade (zenith), base, light (horizon). Three flat bands.

dusk.note: Alternative sky set for a dusk section. Never mix dusk and sky in one layer.

stone.material: Nepean sandstone. Parliament Hill walls and the Peace Tower shaft. Also the cut banks of the Yukon River valley on the-north level, MEASURED at hsl(43,23%,45%) on a 500x150 of assets/refs/the-north/yukon-river-bluff-and-aspen.jpg at (400,400) against stone-base's hsl(36,37%,58%): seven degrees of hue, but fourteen points less saturated and thirteen points darker, because that bank is in haze and in its own shadow. Recorded as the widest gap this ramp is asked to carry rather than rounded away.

limestone.material: Tyndall limestone: the Canadian Museum for Human Rights' stone mass. DELIBERATELY NOT `stone`, which is Nepean sandstone and belongs to Parliament Hill. Base authored from assets/refs/winnipeg/cmhr-elevation-from-the-river.jpg, the median of 240x400 px of sunlit wall at (620,700) = #a99789 = hsl(26,16%,60%); the second reference, winnipeg/cmhr-at-the-forks.jpg, reads hsl(38,12%,58%) through winter haze and is NOT averaged in, because averaging two views is the mistake ADR-0014 records. Light and shade are the published formula. Tyndall is a cool cream-grey at 16 per cent saturation; Nepean sandstone is a golden buff at 41. Two buildings in this game are faced in pale stone and a single ramp for both would make Winnipeg's museum and Ottawa's Parliament the same material.

brick.material: Red-brown facing brick. The Chateau Frontenac's walls, and the Old Quebec brick terraces. Base authored 2026-09-08 from assets/refs/quebec-city/chateau-frontenac-street-elevation.jpg, hue-filtered median of 106441 wall pixels = #a27447 hsl(29,42%,46%) under low warm autumn sun; the same wall in assets/refs/quebec-city/chateau-frontenac-portrait.jpg under overcast winter light medians #735749 hsl(20,21%,37%). The base is set between them and more saturated: hsl(18,52%,44%). It exists because `stone` is Nepean sandstone buff - drawing the Chateau in it would make Quebec City's landmark the same colour as Ottawa's, which is the one confusion this palette must not create.

oxide.material: Red-oxide paint on board-and-batten timber: the prairie grain elevator. Base authored from assets/refs/prairie-rail/grain-elevator-chamberlain.jpg as the HSL midpoint of the two large measured faces - the sunlit driveway annex, median of 300x120 at (120,1080) = hsl(8,73%,36%), and the shaded crib gable, median of 320x560 at (740,620) = hsl(13,63%,32%) - giving hsl(11,68%,34%) = #91301c. NOT `brick`, whose base is hsl(17,52%,44%): eight degrees more orange, sixteen points less saturated and ten points lighter, which under this palette's own three-tone rule turns a painted elevator into a masonry wall. Light and shade are the published formula. MEASURED AGAIN 2026-09-09 for the Bar U Ranch barn on the alberta-foothills level, and NO RAMP WAS ADDED, which is the finding. Six medians on three CC BY 2.0 references - work-horse-barn-elevation.jpg at (500,715) hsl(4,56%,21%) and (900,760) hsl(4,50%,21%); work-horse-barn-gable-end.jpg at (1080,430) hsl(7,54%,18%) and (1250,430) hsl(3,52%,22%); percheron-at-the-barn-wall.jpg at (60,250) hsl(8,51%,26%) and (360,230) hsl(5,37%,23%) - median hsl(5,51%,21%). All three photographs are late-evening or overcast, so the sample is about 13 points of lightness below the material; corrected for the photograph's own light it lands near hsl(6,60%,34%), which is five degrees and eight points of saturation from this ramp's own base at the same lightness. Barn red and elevator red are the same red-oxide paint on the same painted timber, and a second ramp would have been this palette's first duplicate. USED A THIRD TIME 2026-09-13, on the fish stores of the peggys-cove level, with no new measurement and none needed: they are red-oxide paint on board-and-batten timber, which is what this ramp was authored from, on the same construction.

cobalt.material: Deep blue painted joinery and clock dials. The Halifax Town Clock's four dials, which carry gold numerals and gold hands. Base authored 2026-09-08 from assets/refs/halifax/town-clock-elevation.jpg, converted from its embedded profile to sRGB first: the median of 11500 dial pixels in full sun is #113a7b = hsl(217,76%,27%). The base is set at hsl(218,73%,30%), a little lighter and marginally less saturated, so the brass numerals still read at phone size. It exists because `navy` is midnight-blue duty wool at hsl(228,38%,27%) - the same lightness and half the saturation - and a dial painted in it reads dark grey, which loses the one feature this landmark is named for. `sky-shade` was the other candidate and is rejected on principle: an atmosphere ramp is a hand-authored band set, exempt from the derivation formula, and painting a building with one is how a level starts looking like its own sky.

copper.material: Oxidised copper roofing and the Peace Tower spire.

slate.material: Dark metal roofing, bridge steel, lamp posts, skate blades.

ice.material: Rideau Canal skateway ice. Also architectural curtain-wall glazing: the Canadian Museum for Human Rights' glass cloud, measured at hsl(203,41%,80%) sunlit on winnipeg/cmhr-elevation-from-the-river.jpg against ice-base's hsl(202,52%,78%) - one degree of hue apart, which is why no glass ramp was added. Also the North Shore mountains across Burrard Inlet on the vancouver level, measured at hsl(210,48%,65%) and hsl(210,45%,63%) on assets/refs/vancouver/canada-place-and-the-north-shore.jpg against ice-shade's hsl(212,60%,62%) - two degrees of hue and two points of lightness apart - which is the same test that kept the museum's glass out of a ramp of its own. Also the hazy distant headland and the horizon band on the open Atlantic on the peggys-cove level, which is the same use as the North Shore's and needs no new number.

glacier.material: Glacier-fed river water: the Yukon River on the-north level, and the level's second largest colour area after the sky. Base authored 2026-09-13 from two medians on one CC0 reference, assets/refs/the-north/yukon-river-canyon.jpg - 500x150 of mid-channel water at (700,620) = hsl(176,30%,75%) and 400x110 of near water at (200,760) = hsl(169,23%,59%) - giving hsl(172,30%,62%) = #81bbb3. Light and shade are the published formula. IT IS NOT `water`, AND IT IS NOT `copper`, and both were checked rather than argued. `water-base` is hsl(199,62%,45%): twenty-seven degrees of hue, thirty-two points of saturation and seventeen points of lightness away, which is open blue river and lake water and is what four other levels draw. `copper-base` is hsl(162,45%,50%) - ten degrees of hue, fifteen of saturation and twelve of lightness - which is the closest existing tone and is oxidised copper roofing; a river in it would be the Peace Tower's spire spread across a level. The separation from `copper` here is wider than the separation this palette already accepts between `limestone` and `stone` (ten degrees of hue and twenty-one points of saturation), so this ramp is not a duplicate by the palette's own standard. A glacier-fed river is pale, desaturated and green-cyan because it carries rock flour, and no ramp in this palette was that.

pine.material: Conifers, the Christmas-tree lane markers on the skateway. Also black spruce, the boreal forest on the-north level. The measurement is recorded WITH ITS DEFECT: a 600x180 canopy sample on assets/refs/the-north/yukon-river-canyon.jpg at (250,60) reads hsl(70,17%,25%) and a 400x120 on yukon-river-and-spruce.jpg reads hsl(68,25%,32%), which is eighty degrees to the yellow of pine-base's hsl(149,49%,34%) - and both samples contain sunlit deciduous understorey and dry grass between the trunks, which is what a canopy sample of a mixed boreal stand contains. No conifer ramp was added on the strength of a contaminated sample: `pine` is the game's conifer ramp on five levels and a sixth conifer green would be the duplicate this palette refuses.

grass.material: Summer lawn on the Hill. Also the grass that grows in the joints of the granite barrens on the peggys-cove level, where it is the only green and appears only along a joint line, never as a patch on open rock.

pasture.material: Foothills rangeland: the rough-fescue pasture of the Alberta foothills, and the level's largest colour area. Base authored 2026-09-09 from three independent medians on two CC BY 2.0 references - assets/refs/alberta-foothills/foothills-and-front-range.jpg, 350x60 of sunlit near pasture at (1150,520) = hsl(75,35%,38%) and 300x30 of mid pasture at (900,470) = hsl(83,18%,36%), and alberta-foothills/log-rail-fence.jpg, 300x60 of sunlit turf at (1200,800) = hsl(79,40%,29%) - giving hsl(78,38%,35%) = #677b37. Light and shade are the published formula. IT IS NOT `grass`, and that was checked the way `felt` was checked for prairie straw rather than argued: `grass` spans hue 94 (light) to 114 (shade) and every one of the three measurements falls OUTSIDE that span, 11 to 19 degrees to the yellow side. `grass` is the mown summer lawn on Parliament Hill; this is dry native bunchgrass, and one ramp for both would make the Alberta foothills the same material as an Ottawa lawn. `felt` was the other candidate and is rejected in the other direction: its base is hsl(31,49%,55%), which is cut straw, not living grass.

wood.material: Warming huts, benches, lock gates, park signage. Also the paddlewheel, the smokestack and the deck fittings of the sternwheeler on the-north level - a wooden wheel painted ochre, which is what this ramp is. MEASURED on assets/refs/the-north/sternwheeler-paddlewheel.jpg over every pixel with saturation above 35 per cent, hue between 10 and 55 and lightness above 35: median hsl(26,63%,42%) against wood-base's hsl(30,52%,39%) - four degrees of hue and three points of lightness, and eleven points of saturation, the paint being brighter than bare timber. `oxide` was the other candidate and is rejected the same way it was for `brick`: oxide is a red-oxide paint at hsl(11,68%,34%), fifteen degrees to the red and eight points darker, and the wheel is yellow-ochre and not barn red.

path.material: Stone paving, asphalt, concrete. The only near-neutral ramp. Also weathered cedar shingle: the Bar U barn roof medians hsl(20,5%,50%), hsl(26,3%,44%) and hsl(0,1%,50%) across three references against this ramp's base at hsl(31,7%,51%), so the roof is drawn in `path` and no grey was added. AND AGAIN 2026-09-13 for the granite barrens at Peggy's Cove, where the whole walking surface of a level is this ramp, and again NO RAMP WAS ADDED - because four references bracket it. Two clear-day medians on assets/refs/peggys-cove/granite-barrens-and-sea.jpg, 520x60 at (420,470) = hsl(40,23%,71%) and 300x40 at (620,500) = hsl(33,17%,50%), sit two to six degrees of hue and two to four points of lightness from path-light's hsl(42,6%,67%) and path-base's hsl(36,6%,52%) but eleven to seventeen points MORE saturated, which is warm bounce off dry rock in full sun. Two flat-light medians on the same rock - lighthouse-elevation.jpg 400x120 at (600,860) = hsl(0,5%,49%) and lighthouse-on-the-granite.jpg 600x150 at (400,900) = hsl(50,2%,46%) - are one to four points LESS saturated. The ramp sits inside the bracket, and a granite ramp would have been a second near-neutral in a palette whose whole claim is that it has one.

flag-red.material: The National Flag of Canada. See OQ-ART-04. ALSO the lantern room, conical roof and ball finial of Peggy's Point Lighthouse on the peggys-cove level, and the reason is recorded because a red painted on steel and a red on a national flag are not obviously the same red. The reddest decile of the roof cone on assets/refs/peggys-cove/lighthouse-elevation.jpg, 200x36 at (420,176), has median hsl(342,97%,22%) and the lantern's solid panel, 115x34 at (419,262), has median hsl(350,98%,18%). Both are four to eight degrees of hue from flag-red-shade's hsl(346,72%,34%); their saturation at 97 and 98 per cent is that photograph's own edit and not the paint, and it is stated rather than used. `serge`, the palette's other red, is hsl(4,65%,47%) - twenty-two degrees away - so flag-red is the nearer of the two existing reds and a lantern-red ramp would have duplicated it.

navy.material: Midnight-blue duty outerwear, dark trousers, night sky accents.

brass.material: Buckles, buttons, brass hardware, the skateway's amber hazard marks. Also autumn aspen and willow on the-north level. MEASURED on assets/refs/the-north/yukon-river-bluff-and-aspen.jpg: 400x60 at (200,760) = hsl(44,34%,49%) and 300x50 at (1100,750) = hsl(41,30%,49%) against brass-base's hsl(44,69%,50%) - the hue and the lightness match to within three and one, and the saturation gap of thirty-five points is that photograph's own fog bank, which is in frame and is stated rather than corrected away. No gold ramp was added; `felt` is cut straw at hsl(35,47%,55%) and `hair-blond` is hair.

felt.material: Generic tan felt and canvas. Also prairie straw: standing wheat, swath and stubble on the prairie-rail level, measured at hsl(38,63%,33%) on prairie-rail/prairie-harvest-and-shelterbelt.jpg, which sits inside this ramp's own span.

hide.material: Dark bare hide and scale: the beaver's paddle tail, its webbed hind feet and forepaws and its nose, and the moulded rubber sole of a winter boot. Base authored 2026-09-08 from assets/refs/beaver/beaver-paddle-tail.jpg, the only reference in which the paddle is lit, in focus and not in silhouette: the median of 18924 paddle pixels is #293746 = hsl(211,26%,22%). That sample is a WET paddle in low direct sun with sky bounce off wet rock, so it is lighter and bluer than the material; the second reference, beaver-ontario-full-body.jpg, medians the same paddle at #100f13 = hsl(255,12%,7%) and is a colour trap in the other direction - the exposure there is set for snow and the paddle is backlit. The base is authored BETWEEN them at hsl(210,18%,17%), keeping the lit sample's hue and taking a saturation midway between the two, and light and shade are the published formula with no family override (a tail is not skin and its sheen is cool sky, not the red-violet the skin and hair families rotate toward). It exists because nothing in the palette was this: `slate-shade` is hsl(222,24%,25%) and reads as painted bridge steel next to brown fur, `navy-shade` is duty wool, and `hair-black` carries the hair family's 350-degree shade rotation, which would put a red-violet shadow on a wet tail. `leather-shade` was the other candidate and is rejected because a tail drawn in the fur ramp's own shade tone stops being a separate form - and the tail is one of the two features that make a beaver identifiable at phone size.

skin-1.material: Six skin ramps, all derived by the same rule so no tone is 'the default'. The character creator exposes all six. Ordering is lightest to deepest and carries no meaning.

skin-2.material: Six skin ramps, all derived by the same rule so no tone is 'the default'. The character creator exposes all six. Ordering is lightest to deepest and carries no meaning.

skin-3.material: Six skin ramps, all derived by the same rule so no tone is 'the default'. The character creator exposes all six. Ordering is lightest to deepest and carries no meaning.

skin-4.material: Six skin ramps, all derived by the same rule so no tone is 'the default'. The character creator exposes all six. Ordering is lightest to deepest and carries no meaning.

skin-5.material: Six skin ramps, all derived by the same rule so no tone is 'the default'. The character creator exposes all six. Ordering is lightest to deepest and carries no meaning.

skin-6.material: Six skin ramps, all derived by the same rule so no tone is 'the default'. The character creator exposes all six. Ordering is lightest to deepest and carries no meaning.

hair-black.material: Hair. Same three-tone rule as skin.

hair-brown.material: Hair. Same three-tone rule as skin.

hair-blond.material: Hair. Same three-tone rule as skin.

hair-red.material: Hair. Same three-tone rule as skin.

hair-grey.material: Hair. Same three-tone rule as skin.

serge.material: Scarlet review-order tunic wool. Base authored from assets/refs/officer/, sampled #be3828 under warm indoor light and set cooler and more saturated. Deliberately NOT the same red as `flag-red`: the two must not be interchangeable.

white.material: Lanyards, flag field, paper, snow highlight. Clamps at white, so authored.

insignia-rmc-flag.material: The field of the official Royal Military College of Canada flag: the white pale, the two red pales, and the black of the arms' outlines and motto lettering.
insignia-rmc-flag.note: OFFICIAL INSIGNIA, NOT A MATERIAL. These are the colours of the Flag of the Royal Military College of Canada exactly as its official artwork fills them (Commons File:Flag_of_the_Royal_Military_College_of_Canada.svg, sha1 c1f78afdc2ee279fbdf9ac8122ca289716ba016d: Artist of the College of Arms, SVG by Christopher Boucher, 2020; public domain in Canada). The project owner accepted the college flag on kingston's prop-royal-military-college@1x.svg only as the real flag with its real arms, faithful to that artwork (2026-09-26), so its colours are copied, not matched to the nearest house colour: flag-red #d8262c is not the flag's #ed1c24, and a recoloured coat of arms is an approximated insignia, which restrictedMarks names worse than none. The artwork is flat, so these ramps are not lit and not derived: the light/base/shade slots are filled in order of lightness only because a ramp has three slots, and no SVG may use them to cel-shade anything. They may be used by that one flag and by nothing else; any other use is a palette defect. The white is the existing white-light (#ffffff), which the artwork also uses. Commons marks the artwork a prohibited mark (Trademarks Act s. 9(1)(n)(i)); see assets/style/kingston-level.md section 6 and credits.json.

insignia-rmc-crown.material: The crown in the official Royal Military College of Canada arms: gold, the crimson cap (also the wreath's and the scroll ends' red), and the one blue jewel.
insignia-rmc-crown.note: Official insignia, exact and unshaded. See ramps.insignia-rmc-flag.note.

insignia-rmc-crest.material: The crest in the official Royal Military College of Canada arms: the silver armoured arm, the three green maple leaves (also the crown's green jewels), and black outline.
insignia-rmc-crest.note: Official insignia, exact and unshaded. See ramps.insignia-rmc-flag.note.

inks.ink-warm: Characters whose largest area is a warm hue (skin, wood, leather, tan).
inks.ink-cool: Characters whose largest area is a cool hue (navy parka, ice, slate).
inks.ink-neutral: Mixed or neutral characters only. Prefer warm or cool; neutral is the last resort.

note: Palette ids proposed for content/levels/ottawa.json. The level author owns that file.
game.config.schema.json's theme is a vertical gradient: `sky` is the TOP stop and the
renderer clear colour, `ground` is the bottom stop, `horizon` is a rule at two-thirds
height - which is y=1280, the level's ground line. ADR-0002 extends that gradient into the
desktop side panels, so the three ids below are exactly the three flat bands of
assets/src/svg/ottawa/layer-10-sky.svg, in the same order. Authoring them to agree is what
keeps the panel seam invisible, and it is also what lets the sky layer be dropped at the
medium and low visual tiers without the scene losing its sky (ADR-0011).
`sky` is sky-shade rather than sky-base because it is the zenith, not the mid band.

quebec-city-winter.why: Deliberately NOT Ottawa's set. Ottawa's zenith is `sky-shade` over a `sky-light` horizon: a deep, clear, cold blue. Quebec City is a paler, hazier winter afternoon - `sky-base` at the zenith fading to a `cloud-base` haze at the horizon rule - which is what assets/refs/quebec-city/quebec-ramparts-snow.jpg and quebec-city-waterfront-winter.jpg both show, and which keeps two winter levels from looking like the same level.

skyBandStops.note: Design-resolution y at which layer-10-sky.svg changes band, matching the three gradient stops in order so the medium and low presets can drop the sky layer without the scene losing its sky (ADR-0011).
Design-resolution y at which layer-10-sky.svg changes band. Both edges sit behind a nearer layer at the high tier so the hard step never shows against open sky.

winnipeg-autumn.why: A deep, clear, dry continental blue over a river promenade in early autumn. Measured on assets/refs/winnipeg/cmhr-elevation-from-the-river.jpg: 300x200 px of open sky at (800,100) reads hsl(210,83%,41%) against sky-shade's hsl(212,69%,39%). The ground is limestone-shade so that the band the player walks on continues the promenade's own material into the fill below the ground line, which is the arrangement Halifax uses and the reason its deck stopped reading as a road. No two of the six level triples are equal.

skyBandStops.note: NONE. winnipeg/layer-10-sky.svg is ONE FLAT sky-shade field and has no band steps at all. A banded sky needs every step to sit behind a nearer opaque layer at every visual tier, and at the LOW preset this level keeps only the sky and the plaza, whose opaque paving does not begin until world 1150 - so there was nowhere above it to hide a step. The flat field IS the level document's theme.sky, so dropping the layer changes nothing above the roofline.

prairie-rail-late-summer.why: The palest sky in the game and the largest, because on the prairie the sky is most of the picture. Measured on assets/refs/prairie-rail/grain-elevator-chamberlain.jpg: 300x200 px of open sky at (100,100) reads hsl(213,50%,61%), between sky-base and sky-light, and sky-light is taken so that the horizon band can go to cloud-light without a visible step. Shares its zenith with Toronto and its horizon with Halifax; the ground - dark straw rather than pavement - is what keeps all three apart.

skyBandStops.note: NONE. prairie-rail/layer-10-sky.svg is ONE FLAT sky-light field. Same reason as Winnipeg's, and harder: at the LOW preset this level keeps the sky and the railbed, and the railbed is transparent everywhere above the rail head, so there is no opaque layer anywhere in the sky's band to hide a step behind.

alberta-foothills-late-summer.why: A deep, dry continental blue over foothills rangeland in late summer. MEASURED on assets/refs/alberta-foothills/rangeland-cattle-and-wire-fence.jpg: 1200x60 of open sky at (200,20) reads hsl(214,47%,43%) against sky-shade's hsl(212,69%,39%), and 1200x40 of the haze band at (200,420) reads hsl(215,18%,71%) against cloud-shade's hsl(206,44%,80%) - nine points of lightness apart, which is the largest gap of any horizon in the game and is recorded rather than rounded away, because an atmosphere ramp is hand-authored and exempt from the derivation formula. The ground is the pasture's own turf in shadow, which is the arrangement Halifax arrived at the hard way. This is the third triple whose zenith is sky-shade and no two of the eight triples differ in only one of their three.

skyBandStops.note: NONE. alberta-foothills/layer-10-sky.svg is ONE FLAT sky-shade field. Same reason as Winnipeg's and the Prairies': at the LOW preset this level keeps the sky and the rangeland, and the rangeland is transparent everywhere above its own grass horizon at world 1130, so there is no opaque layer inside the sky's band to hide a band step behind.

vancouver-pacific-afternoon.why: A clear marine afternoon over Burrard Inlet, paling toward a bright horizon over the water. The zenith is authored BETWEEN two references that disagree and both are recorded: 600x40 of open sky at (600,15) on assets/refs/vancouver/canada-place-from-the-west.jpg reads hsl(218,49%,30%) and 700x40 at (400,40) on seawall-path-and-harbour.jpg reads hsl(204,99%,47%); sky-base is hsl(206,58%,52%) and is taken toward the brighter because this level is an afternoon on the water. The horizon is sky-light against the second reference's low sky at hsl(208,91%,70%). THE GROUND IS TORONTO'S, and that is allowed rather than overlooked: the rule this palette keeps is that no two triples are equal and no triple differs from another in only ONE of its three, and (sky-base, sky-light) differs from Toronto's (sky-light, cloud-base) in both of the other two. Both levels are city waterfront paving and both grounds are that paving in shadow.

skyBandStops.note: NONE. vancouver/layer-10-sky.svg is ONE FLAT sky-base field, for the same reason as the three levels above it. Its clouds are high CIRRUS rather than cumulus, which is what refs/vancouver/seawall-path-and-harbour.jpg shows and is the only sky of its kind in the game.

peggys-cove-atlantic-morning.why: A clear morning on the Atlantic coast over pale granite. The zenith is MEASURED: 400x60 of open sky at (60,60) on assets/refs/peggys-cove/granite-barrens-and-sea.jpg has median hsl(204,47%,54%) against sky-base's hsl(207,58%,52%) - three degrees of hue and two points of lightness. THE GROUND IS PATH-LIGHT AND NO OTHER LEVEL USES IT: Halifax's ground is path-base, Toronto's and Vancouver's are path-shade, and this one is the palest of the three because the surface the player walks on is sunlit bare granite, measured at hsl(40,23%,71%) against path-light's hsl(42,6%,67%). The horizon is ice-base against the sea haze rather than a cloud tone, which is the only unused pale band left: sky-light would have made this triple differ from Vancouver's in only one of its three, cloud-light from Halifax's in only one, and cloud-base from Quebec City's in only one. That rule is why the ninth triple took three attempts and it is recorded so the tenth does not repeat them. MEASURED ACROSS ALL TEN TRIPLES ON 2026-09-13, AND THE RULE IS ALREADY BROKEN TWICE — by two levels that shipped before either of today's. `ottawa` (sky-base, snow-base, sky-light) differs from `quebec-city` (sky-base, snow-base, cloud-base) in ONE of its three, and from `vancouver` (sky-base, path-shade, sky-light) in ONE. Neither of today's two triples violates it against any of the other nine. The finding is recorded here rather than quietly satisfied: a rule that two shipped levels fail is either the wrong rule or two levels needing a theme edit, and that is the project owner's to settle, not an artist drawing the tenth level.

skyBandStops.note: NONE. peggys-cove/layer-10-sky.svg is ONE FLAT sky-base field, for the same reason as Winnipeg's, the Prairies', the Alberta foothills' and Vancouver's: at the LOW preset this level keeps the sky and the granite barrens, and the barrens tile is transparent everywhere above its own crest line at world 1024, so there is no nearer opaque layer inside this band to hide a band step behind. The flat field IS the level document's theme.sky. Its clouds are STRATOCUMULUS ROLLS - lumpy-topped, flat-based bars in rows - which is the sixth distinct cloud treatment in the game and the only one of its kind.

the-north-late-summer.why: A deep, clear, cold high-latitude sky over a glacier-fed river and a gravel bar. The zenith is sky-shade, which Winnipeg and the Alberta foothills also take, and the triple is kept apart by the other two: the ground is the gravel bar's own cobble, which is path-base - Halifax's ground, over a different sky and a different horizon - and the horizon is snow-shade, which no other level uses at all. That is two of three different from every one of the other nine, which is the rule. The horizon is a cold pale haze rather than a cloud tone because at this latitude the band above the far ridge is ice-blue and not white. The same all-ten check that cleared this triple found two PRE-EXISTING violations of the rule, between `ottawa` and `quebec-city` and between `ottawa` and `vancouver`; they are written out in levelTheme.peggys-cove-atlantic-morning and neither is today's to fix.

skyBandStops.note: NONE. the-north/layer-10-sky.svg is ONE FLAT sky-shade field, for the reason Winnipeg's, the Prairies', the Alberta foothills', Vancouver's and Peggy's Cove's are: at the LOW preset this level keeps the sky and the river-and-bar tile, and that tile's first opaque row is world 960, so a band step anywhere above it would show against open sky. Its clouds are LENTICULAR STACKS - smooth stacked lens shapes, the mountain-wave cloud of a high range - which is the seventh distinct cloud treatment in the game and the only one with a vertical stack in it.

kingston-lakeshore-summer.why: A clear summer afternoon on Lake Ontario over a city of grey limestone. `sky-base` at the zenith, the lake's `sky-light` haze at the horizon rule, and the ground is `path-light` because Kingston's limestone measures grey (sunlit hsl(55, 7 %, 68 %) on assets/refs/kingston/city-hall-dome-and-clocks-2011.jpg) and the paving strip the player walks on is that stone, so the ground polygon and the strip meet with no step. Deliberately not Toronto's (`sky-light`, `path-shade`, `cloud-base`), which is the same lake a level later under a bleached city haze over asphalt. No two level triples are equal.

skyBandStops.note: Design-resolution y at which layer-10-sky.svg changes band. The one step sits behind the opaque water of layer-30-harbour, which starts at world 900 and is the layer kept beside the sky at every tier, the low preset included, so it never shows against open sky.

restrictedMarks.why: The officer NPC wears the recognisable red-serge silhouette. That silhouette is not a protected mark and is what carries the recognition. The insignia are protected, and their absence is a deliberate constraint with a legal reason, not a stylistic choice. Decided by the user on 2026-09-08 after the licensing risk was raised.
neverDraw: any crest or badge, including the bison-head device
any wordmark or lettering: RCMP, GRC, Royal Canadian Mounted Police, Gendarmerie royale du Canada
collar dogs, shoulder flashes, rank chevrons, service numbers
an approximation of any of the above - an approximated insignia is worse than none, because it reads as an attempt at the real thing
restrictedMarks.naming: Never 'RCMP Officer' and never a member of a named force. Generic: 'Constable', or a personal name. Copy belongs to the PO; this is the constraint the copy must satisfy.
